newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares open weak, seen in tight range.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares open weak, seen in tight range.

text.p: Russian shares opened quietly on Thursday and traders predicted the market would be bound to a range of about 1.5 percent for the day as investors waited developments in the restructuring of bellwether UES.

"There is nothing to tell investors that this is the bottom," said Dan Rapoport, director of institutional sales at CentreInvest Securities. "Yesterday we thought that had happened, but (the flow of funds) was unsustained."

The Russian Trading System 23-share index opened at 303.39 after closing at 303.34 on Wednesday. Volume was seen lower than Wednesday's $41 million, a healthy day, after a couple of weeks of thin trading, which saw a five percent RTS index gain.

UES EESR.RTS had eased to $0.2040 at 0825 GMT on the Russian Trading System (RTS) from $0.2100 at Wednesday's close. Traders said investors who had poured funds into the stock midweek had paused for consideration.
The government intends to reform UES, Russia's largest company by sales, and First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov has begun to speak publicly of his plans this week.
LUKoil LKOH.RTS oil producer had fallen to $13.65 from $13.80.
"It is not going to go up in a straight line," said Brunswick director Martin Diggle. "If UES appreciates, the rest of the market will follow."

Dealers said regional utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS had recovered from a sell-off after the company announced it would consider moves to limit foreign participation and dilute equity at its annual meeting on April 21.
One dealer at a Western firm said the market had priced in the amendments passing.

Mosenergo, one of the top 10 shares by turnover, had edged up to $1.220 from $1.214. It was about $1.12 at the beginning of the week, falling from near $1.33 when it announced the proposed amendments on March 24.
